theory.intro: A frequency table organises data into categories with the count (frequency) of each.
facts: **Frequency** is how many times a value or category appears.
The frequencies should add up to the **total** number of results.
Tally marks can be turned into frequencies, then totalled.
steps: List each category or value in the first column.
Add the frequencies to check the total.

workedExamples.question_text:
The colours of cars passing a school were recorded:
Red, Blue, White, Blue, Red, White, Blue, Red, Blue.
Construct a frequency table and check its total.
workedExamples.solution_text:
List each colour and count how often it appears.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Car colour}&\text{Frequency}\\\hline\text{Red}&3\\\text{Blue}&4\\\text{White}&2\end{array}$
Check: $3+4+2=9$, matching the nine recorded cars.

workedExamples.question_text:
These scores were recorded:
$2,0,3,1,2,3,0,2,1,3,2,1$.
Construct a frequency table and check that its total equals the number of scores.
workedExamples.solution_text:
List the scores in increasing order, then count each score.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Score}&\text{Frequency}\\\hline0&2\\1&3\\2&4\\3&3\end{array}$
A score of $0$ is a recorded result, so count it too.
Check: $2+3+4+3=12$, matching the twelve scores.

workedExamples.question_text:
A student records car colours using the categories Red, Blue, White and Green.
The observations are:
White, Red, Blue, White, Blue, White, Red, Blue, White, Blue.
Construct a frequency table with a row for every named category and check its total.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Count each named category. Keep Green in the table even though no green cars were recorded.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Car colour}&\text{Frequency}\\\hline\text{Red}&2\\\text{Blue}&4\\\text{White}&4\\\text{Green}&0\end{array}$
Green has frequency $0$.
Check: $2+4+4+0=10$, matching the ten observations.

foundation.question_text:
These library loans were recorded: Fiction, Non-fiction, Fiction, Graphic novel, Fiction, Non-fiction.
Make a frequency table.

The numbers of people in six families are: $3,4,2,3,4,3$.
Construct a frequency distribution table.

The numbers of people in eight families are: $2,5,3,2,4,3,5,3$.
Construct a frequency distribution table.

These scores were recorded: $0,2,1,2,3,1,2,0,3,2$.
Construct a frequency table and check that its total equals the number of scores.
foundation.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Score}&\text{Frequency}\\ \hline 0&2\\1&2\\2&4\\3&2\end{array}$
Check: $2+2+4+2=10$, which equals the number of scores.

foundation.question_text:
A library tracks loans from four sections: Animals, Space, Sport and Art.
Today's loans were: Animals, Art, Animals, Space, Animals, Art, Space, Animals, Art.
Make a frequency table with a row for every named section.
foundation.solution_text:
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Category}&\text{Frequency}\\ \hline \text{Animals}&4\\ \text{Space}&2\\ \text{Sport}&0\\ \text{Art}&3\end{array}$
Check: $4+2+0+3=9$. Sport has frequency $0$ because it does not appear in the observations.

These loans were recorded: Dinosaurs, Oceans, Plants, Dinosaurs, Oceans, Dinosaurs, Plants, Oceans, Dinosaurs, Plants, Dinosaurs, Oceans.
